why: Caffeine can make it harder to fall asleep or sleep well, but sensitivity, dose, timing, medications, pregnancy, and health conditions all matter.

slides.title: Timing Is Personal
slides.content: Caffeine can remain active for hours. An afternoon cutoff may help, but there is no single clock time that fits everyone.

slides.title: Notice Dose and Timing
slides.content: Coffee, tea, energy drinks, some soft drinks, chocolate, supplements, and medications may contain caffeine.

slides.title: Protect the Wind-Down
slides.content: If sleep is difficult, try moving your last caffeine earlier or reducing the amount rather than chasing one perfect rule.

slides.title: Look for Your Pattern
slides.content: Track caffeine timing alongside how long it takes to fall asleep, nighttime waking, and how rested you feel.

slides.title: Avoid Absolutes
slides.content: Feeling able to fall asleep does not tell the whole story, but one caffeinated drink does not guarantee a poor night either.

slides.title: Try a Small Experiment
slides.content: For several days, keep the rest of your routine steady and move your last caffeine earlier. Notice whether sleep or daytime energy changes.
